title.narrative: Scaling Up Anticipatory Actions for Drought Hazard Management in Legehida and Sewan woredas of Oromia Region, Ethiopia

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Anticipatory Action Program in the Oromia region of Ethiopia addresses the critical drought conditions forecasted by the EDRMC’s early warning report (September 20, 2024). Projections indicate severe drought during the October-December rains, particularly affecting the Legehida and Sewan woredas. Approximately 186,837 individuals—mainly from vulnerable pastoral and agropastoral communities—are at risk of significant impacts on their livelihoods, health, and nutrition.ltbrgtThis anticipated drought, driven by La Niña conditions, threatens to reduce water and pasture availability, diminish crop yields, and compromise livestock health. Consequently, this will likely lead to increased food prices and heightened malnutrition. Many households are still struggling to recover from the severe drought experienced from 2020 to 2023, and recent shocks, such as flooding, have further hindered recovery efforts.ltbrgtIn partnership with the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS), Save the Children (SC) is seeking support from the Emergency Humanitarian Fund (EHF) to implement anticipatory actions aimed at mitigating the anticipated impacts before they escalate. This initiative aligns with the 2024 second Reserve Allocation Strategy and the Ethiopia Humanitarian Response Plan, focusing on WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), Health, and Nutrition cluster priorities.ltbrgtThe project adopts an area-based, intersectoral approach, promoting localization and enhancing collaboration between SC and ERCS to maximize program effectiveness and community resilience. Key actions include providing multi-purpose cash assistance, strengthening animal health services, and promoting irrigation-based agriculture. Accountability is a priority, ensured through community consultations, transparent communication, and robust feedback mechanisms. Gender equality, inclusion, protection, and issues related to GBV will be mainstreamed throughout all project phases.ltbrgtBy leveraging best practices from previous initiatives and fostering government engagement, this program aims to protect the livelihoods of vulnerable communities, reaching a total of 257,387 beneficiaries with a budget of $500,000 for the Legehida and Sewan woredas over a six-month duration. Through these efforts, we aspire to mitigate the worst effects of drought and enhance the overall resilience of communities in the Oromia region of Ethiopia.ltbrgtlt/pgt
